title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Effects of vitamins C and E supplementation combined with 12-week resistance training in older women with sarcopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Xu Liu, Bo Chen, Yutian Jin, Feiyan Zhong, Yunjuan Zhang, Yu Li, Yun Zhang, Runhong Cui, Bing Wu, Cu...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C, E, and resistance training in older women with sarcopenia. Supplementation with vitamins C and E enhanced muscle mass and strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Does vitamin-D intake during resistance training improve the skeletal muscle hypertrophic and strength response in young and elderly men? – a randomized controlled trial
authors: Jakob Agergaard, Jeanette Trøstrup, Jacob Uth, Jonas Vestergard Iversen, Anders Boesen, Jesper L. An...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin-D's impact on muscle growth and strength during resistance training in young and elderly men. Vitamin-D supplementation did not enhance muscle hypertrophy or strength gains, though some molecular changes were observed in young men.

title: Effects of Resistance Training Combined with Vitamin D Supplementation on Health-Related Variables in the Elderly: Muscle Strength, Body Composition, and Inflammatory Status
authors: Lorena Cristina Ribeiro da Rosa, Paulo de Tarso Veras Farinatti, Maria Izabel Ferreira Batista, Hile...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study examined the effects of resistance training plus vitamin D supplementation on older adults. The combination did not improve strength, body composition, or inflammation more than resistance training alone.

title: Vitamin D 3  supplementation does not enhance the effects of resistance training in older adults
authors: Knut Sindre Mølmen, Daniel Hammarström, Karianne Pedersen, Anne Cecilie Lian Lie, Ragnvald B. Steile...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation on resistance training outcomes in older adults. Vitamin D3 supplementation did not enhance improvements in muscle strength, mass, or endurance compared to placebo.

title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: The effect of combined resistance exercise training and vitamin D 3  supplementation on musculoskeletal health and function in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Antoniak, Carolyn A Greig
abstract: This systematic review evaluated combined resistance exercise and vitamin D supplementation in older adults. The combination significantly improved lower limb muscle strength compared to exercise alone.

title: Effects of Vitamin D3 Supplementation and Resistance Training on 25-Hydroxyvitamin D Status and Functional Performance of Older Adults: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Rudolf Aschauer, Sandra Unterberger, Patrick A. Zöhrer, Agnes Draxler, Bernhard Franzke, Eva-Maria S...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation and resistance training on older adults. Vitamin D supplementation improved vitamin D status but did not enhance muscle performance or functional mobility beyond resistance training alone.

title: Can Low-Dose of Dietary Vitamin E Supplementation Reduce Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress? A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Myunghee Kim, Hyeyoon Eo, Josephine Gahyun Lim, Hyunjung Lim, Yunsook Lim
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effects of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage. Low-dose vitamin E, especially under 500 IU, was found to reduce muscle damage, particularly in athletes.

title: Influence of combined vitamin D 3  supplementation and resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older men and women (EXVITD): protocol for a randomised controlled trial
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Welford, Susan Lanham-New, Janet Lord, Alison Doyle, Julie Robinson, Peter Nighting...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial investigates the effect of vitamin D3 supplementation combined with resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older adults. The study aims to determine if this combination improves muscle function more than exercise training alone.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Does Not Enhance Gains in Muscle Strength and Lean Body Mass or Influence Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Vitamin D-Insufficient Middle-Aged Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Evelin Mäestu, Luule Medijainen, Märt Lellsaar, Kri...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D supplementation's effect on resistance training outcomes in vitamin D-insufficient men. Vitamin D supplementation did not enhance muscle strength, lean body mass, or cardiorespiratory fitness gains.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: Four months vitamin D supplementation to vitamin D insufficient individuals does not improve muscular strength: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Guri Grimnes, Julia Kubiak, Rolf Jorde
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin D supplementation on muscle strength in vitamin D insufficient individuals. Four months of supplementation did not improve muscle strength compared to placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation and high intensity interval training induced changes in lipid profile and haematological variables of young males
authors: Surojit Sarkar, Swapan Kr Dey, Gouriprosad Datta, Amit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in young males. Supplementation protected against negative hematological changes and improved lipid profiles and explosive strength without affecting endurance.

title: The role of resistance training and creatine supplementation on oxidative stress, antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life in older adults
authors: Ehsan Amiri, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani
abstract: Resistance training with creatine supplementation was studied in older adults. This intervention improved antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life, with creatine enhancing strength gains.

title: The Effects of Strength Training Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Maurilio T. Dutra, Wagner Rodrigues Martins, Alexandre L. A. Ribeiro, Martim Bottaro
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined studies on vitamin C and E supplementation combined with strength training. The findings suggest these supplements do not enhance muscle strength or mass and may even attenuate hypertrophy.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Antioxidants and Exercise Performance: With a Focus on Vitamin E and C Supplementation
authors: Madalyn Riley Higgins, Azimeh Izadi, Mojtaba Kaviani
abstract: This paper reviews antioxidant supplementation, specifically vitamins E and C, for exercise performance. Evidence suggests supplementation may hinder exercise adaptations and is generally not beneficial, except in specific circumstances.

title: Effect of high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle recovery and training adaptation: a mini review
authors: Jooyoung Kim
abstract: This review examined high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle recovery and training adaptation. Evidence suggests potential negative impacts on adaptation, with unclear benefits for recovery.

title: Do Antioxidant Vitamins Prevent Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage? A Systematic Review
authors: María Martinez-Ferran, Fabian Sanchis-Gomar, Carl J. Lavie, Giuseppe Lippi, Helios Pareja-Galeano
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle damage. The available data are not conclusive regarding whether these vitamins prevent muscle damage.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on upper and lower limb muscle strength and muscle power in athletes: A meta-analysis
authors: Lin Zhang, Minghui Quan, Zhen-Bo Cao
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of vitamin D supplementation on athlete muscle strength and power. Vitamin D supplementation positively impacted lower limb muscle strength, but not upper limb strength or muscle power.

title: Supplementation with Vitamins C and E and Exercise-Induced Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review
authors: María F. Torre, María Martinez-Ferran, Néstor Vallecillo, Sergio L. Jiménez, Carlos Romero-Morales, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effect on exercise-induced muscle soreness. The evidence is insufficient to confirm these vitamins minimize delayed-onset muscle soreness.

title: The Effect of Nordic Walking Training Combined with Vitamin D Supplementation on Postural Control and Muscle Strength in Elderly People—A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Jan Mieszkowski, Bartłomiej Niespodziński, Andrzej Kochanowicz, Anna Gmiat, Krzysztof Prusik, Katarz...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of Nordic Walking intensity and Vitamin D supplementation on elderly women. High-intensity Nordic Walking improved Vitamin D and muscle strength, while moderate-intensity Nordic Walking showed similar Vitamin D benefits with higher supplementation, also increasing leg muscle mass.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Effects of daily vitamin D supplementation on respiratory muscle strength and physical performance in vitamin D-deficient COPD patients: a pilot trial
authors: Rachida Rafiq, Hendrik J Prins, Wim G Boersma, Johannes MA Daniels, Martin den Heijer, Paul Lips, Re...
source: International Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
abstract: This pilot trial investigated daily vitamin D supplementation in vitamin D-deficient COPD patients. Supplementation did not significantly improve respiratory muscle strength or physical performance after six months.

title: Effects of Insect Protein Supplementation during Resistance Training on Changes in Muscle Mass and Strength in Young Men
authors: Mathias T. Vangsoe, Malte S. Joergensen, Lars-Henrik L. Heckmann, Mette Hansen
abstract: This study investigated insect protein supplementation's effects on muscle mass and strength during resistance training. Insect protein did not show superior benefits compared to carbohydrate supplementation for muscle adaptations in young men.

title: Muscle-Related Effect of Whey Protein and Vitamin D 3  Supplementation Provided before or after Bedtime in Males Undergoing Resistance Training
authors: Yan Chen, Yiheng Liang, Hang Guo, Kun Meng, Junqiang Qiu, Dan Benardot
abstract: This study examined the effects of whey protein and vitamin D supplementation before or after sleep on muscle mass and strength during resistance training. Both supplementation timings led to significant improvements in muscle mass and hormones compared to a placebo.

title: Effects of free leucine supplementation and resistance training on muscle strength and functional status in older adults: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Joan Trabal, Maria Forga, Pere Leyes, Ferran Torres, Jordi Rubio, Esther Prieto, Andreu Farran-Codin...
abstract: This study investigated leucine supplementation with resistance training in older adults. Leucine supplementation, combined with resistance training, showed a greater positive effect on leg strength and some functional measures compared to resistance training alone.

title: Effects of ascorbic acid supplementation on oxidative stress markers in healthy women following a single bout of exercise
authors: Manita Yimcharoen, Suwatsin Kittikunnathum, Chawannut Suknikorn, Wichuda Nak-on, Petcharee Yeethong,...
abstract: This study investigated ascorbic acid's effects on oxidative stress markers in women after exercise. Ascorbic acid improved antioxidant capacity but did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

title: Human skeletal muscle ascorbate is highly responsive to changes in vitamin C intake and plasma concentrations 1 2 3
authors: Anitra C Carr, Stephanie M Bozonet, Juliet M Pullar, Jeremy W Simcock, Margreet CM Vissers
abstract: Skeletal muscle ascorbate levels were studied in response to vitamin C intake from kiwifruit. Muscle ascorbate concentrations significantly increased with intake and were more responsive than leukocytes.

title: Effect of an herbal/botanical supplement on strength, balance, and muscle function following 12-weeks of resistance training: a placebo controlled study
authors: Jonathan Furlong, Corey A Rynders, Mark Sutherlin, James Patrie, Frank I Katch, Jay Hertel, Arthur W...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: A 12-week resistance training program was studied with and without an herbal supplement. The supplement did not enhance strength, balance, or muscle function adaptations beyond those from training alone.

title: Collagen peptide supplementation in combination with resistance training improves body composition and increases muscle strength in elderly sarcopenic men: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Denise Zdzieblik, Steffen Oesser, Manfred W. Baumstark, Albert Gollhofer, Daniel König
abstract: This study investigated collagen peptide supplementation alongside resistance training in elderly men with sarcopenia. Collagen peptide supplementation, combined with resistance training, significantly improved body composition and muscle strength more than placebo.

title: Astaxanthin-, β-Carotene-, and Resveratrol-Rich Foods Support Resistance Training-Induced Adaptation
authors: Aki Kawamura, Wataru Aoi, Ryo Abe, Yukiko Kobayashi, Masashi Kuwahata, Akane Higashi
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with nutrient-rich foods on muscle adaptation in men. Consuming foods rich in astaxanthin, β-carotene, and resveratrol enhanced strength and metabolic improvements from training.

title: Complex Effects of Vitamin E and Vitamin C Supplementation on  in Vitro  Neonatal Mononuclear Cell Responses to Allergens
authors: Heather J. H. Wassall, Graham Devereux, Anthony Seaton, Robert N. Barker
abstract: This study examined how vitamin E and C supplementation affects neonatal immune cells' response to allergens. Vitamin E showed complex effects, sometimes reducing proliferation and other times increasing it, while vitamin C had varied impacts on cytokine production.

title: The effect of an acute antioxidant supplementation compared with placebo on performance and hormonal response during a high volume resistance training session
authors: James Ackerman, Tom Clifford, Lars R McNaughton, David J Bentley
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: An antioxidant supplement was compared to a placebo before a high-volume resistance training session. The antioxidant group showed improved muscle performance and a blunted growth hormone response.

title: Lower Dietary and Circulating Vitamin C in Middle- and Older-Aged Men and Women Are Associated with Lower Estimated Skeletal Muscle Mass
authors: Lucy N Lewis, Richard P G Hayhoe, Angela A Mulligan, Robert N Luben, Kay-Tee Khaw, Ailsa A Welch
abstract: This study examined the relationship between vitamin C intake and levels with skeletal muscle mass in middle-aged and older adults. Lower dietary and circulating vitamin C were associated with lower estimated skeletal muscle mass.

title: Effects of 8 weeks of Xpand® 2X pre workout supplementation on skeletal muscle hypertrophy, lean body mass, and strength in resistance trained males
authors: Ryan P Lowery, Jordan M Joy, Joshua E Dudeck, Eduardo Oliveira de Souza, Sean A McCleary, Shawn Well...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an 8-week pre-workout supplement on resistance-trained males. The supplement significantly increased bench press strength, lean body mass, and quadriceps muscle thickness compared to a placebo.

title: Effects of a combined protein and antioxidant supplement on recovery of muscle function and soreness following eccentric exercise
authors: Stephen J. Ives, Samuel Bloom, Alexs Matias, Noelle Morrow, Natalya Martins, Yookee Roh, Daniel Eben...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined protein and antioxidant supplementation on muscle recovery after eccentric exercise. The combined supplement improved muscle soreness more than protein or carbohydrate alone.

title: Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Performance: “Common Knowledge” vs. Experimental Evidence
authors: Andrés Hernández, Arthur Cheng, Håkan Westerblad
abstract: This paper reviews experimental evidence on the effects of antioxidants on skeletal muscle performance. Findings suggest that common beliefs about antioxidant benefits may not be supported by scientific data and could potentially be harmful.

title: Resistance-based training improves mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in aging adults, independent of polyphenol supplementation
authors: Mathias Flensted-Jensen, Cecilie Moe Weinreich, Ann-Sofie Kleis-Olsen, Filip Hansen, Nadia Stenner S...
abstract: Resistance training improved mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in older adults. Polyphenol supplementation did not enhance these adaptations and may have altered some vitamin responses.

title: The effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on skeletal muscle and strength adaptations in older individuals
authors: Donald A. Lamb, Johnathon H. Moore, Morgan A. Smith, Christopher G. Vann, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on muscle and strength in older adults. Peanut protein supplementation showed some benefits in muscle thickness and strength, but not overall body composition or acute muscle protein synthesis.

title: Modification of the Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on the Mortality of Male Smokers by Age and Dietary Vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: Vitamin E supplementation's effect on mortality in male smokers was examined. Its impact varied significantly by age and dietary vitamin C intake, suggesting heterogeneous effects in different population subgroups.

title: Resistance-Trained Individuals Are Less Susceptible to Oxidative Damage after Eccentric Exercise
authors: Ypatios Spanidis, Dimitrios Stagos, Christina Papanikolaou, Konstantina Karatza, Andria Theodosi, Ar...
abstract: Resistance-trained individuals experienced less oxidative damage and had a stronger antioxidant profile after eccentric exercise compared to untrained individuals. This suggests training status significantly influences exercise-induced oxidative stress and recovery.

title: Redox correlation in muscle lengthening and immune response in eccentric exercise
authors: Feng He, Chia-Chen Chuang, Tingyang Zhou, Qing Jiang, Darlene A. Sedlock, Li Zuo
abstract: Eccentric exercise in mice and humans was studied for its effects on muscle function and immune cells. Antioxidant supplementation attenuated exercise-induced changes in anti-apoptotic proteins and may protect against muscle dysfunction.

title: VITADIAL “Does correction of 25 OH-VITAmin D with cholecalciferol supplementation increase muscle strength in hemoDIALysis patients?”: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Stanislas Bataille, Nathalie Pedinielli, Elisa Carreno, Mathilde Prezelin-Reydit, Philippe Chauveau,...
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating if cholecalciferol supplementation improves muscle strength in hemodialysis patients with low vitamin D. The primary finding will be whether this supplementation leads to increased muscle strength over six months.

title: Antioxidant Effects and Insulin Resistance Improvement of Chromium Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Ming-Hoang Lai
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of chromium, vitamin C, and E supplementation on type 2 diabetes patients. Combined supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress and improved glucose metabolism.

title: The impact of nutritional intervention and resistance training on muscle strength and mass in healthy older adults—a comparative analysis
authors: Yongye Ma, Ruixiang Yan, Yueming Li, Duanying Li, Xiaoning Sun, Tao Chen, Xingyu Liu
abstract: This study compared nutritional interventions with resistance training in older adults. Protein supplementation combined with resistance training significantly improved muscle strength and mass, while creatine showed the most pronounced muscle mass gains.

title: Effect of Vitamins C and E Co-Supplementation on Serum C-Reactive Protein Level: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Faezeh Fouladvand, Ebrahim Falahi, Omid Asbaghi, Amir Abbasnezhad
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined vitamin C and E co-supplementation's effect on C-reactive protein. Co-supplementation did not significantly impact CRP overall, but reduced it in those aged 30 and over.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: The Effect of Combined Vitamin C and Vitamin E Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Markers in Women with Endometriosis: A Randomized, Triple-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Leila Amini, Razieh Chekini, Mohammad Reza Nateghi, Hamid Haghani, Tannaz Jamialahmadi, Thozhukat Sa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C and E supplementation on oxidative stress and pain in women with endometriosis. The supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and pelvic pain symptoms.

title: Antioxidant supplements and endurance exercise: Current evidence and mechanistic insights
authors: Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Lewan Parker, Glenn D. Wadley
abstract: This review examines antioxidant supplements for endurance athletes. Most supplements lack evidence for performance enhancement, with some potentially hindering training adaptations.

title: Vitamin D supplementation and increased dairy protein intake do not affect muscle strength or physical function in healthy 6–8-year-old children: the  D-pro  randomized trial
authors: Line Thams, Lars G. Hvid, Nanna G. Stounbjerg, Jan C. Brønd, Christian Mølgaard, Camilla T. Damsgaar...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D and increased dairy protein intake's effects on children's muscle strength and physical function. Neither intervention, alone or combined, improved these measures in healthy children.

title: Vitamin C Is Essential for the Maintenance of Skeletal Muscle Functions
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Yuka Takino, Jaewon Lee, Shuichi Machida, Akihito Ishigami
abstract: Long-term vitamin C deficiency was studied in male mice lacking VC synthesis, showing muscle atrophy and reduced physical ability. Vitamin C is essential for maintaining skeletal muscle function in both sexes.

title: Low‐Dose Lemon Myrtle Supplementation Enhances Muscle Hypertrophy in Older Adults Undergoing Low‐Load Resistance Training: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Risa Mitsuhashi, Shuji Sawada, Azusa Nishino, Shinichi Honda, Yuji Tominaga, Shiori Makio, Hayao Oza...
abstract: Low-dose lemon myrtle supplementation was studied with low-load resistance training in older adults. The supplement enhanced muscle growth after training but did not maintain it during detraining.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Markers of Oxidative Stress and Muscle Damage after Strength Exercise: A Systematic Review
authors: Cristina Canals-Garzón, Rafael Guisado-Barrilao, Darío Martínez-García, Ignacio Jesús Chirosa-Ríos, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined antioxidant supplementation's effects on oxidative stress and muscle damage after strength exercise. Antioxidants like pomegranate juice and taurine showed beneficial effects, potentially reducing fatigue and speeding recovery.

title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
authors: Robert W Morton, Kevin T Murphy, Sean R McKellar, Brad J Schoenfeld, Menno Henselmans, Eric Helms, A...
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis examined protein supplementation's effect on resistance training gains. Protein supplementation significantly increased muscle mass and strength, with benefits varying by age and training experience.

title: Low-Frequency Fatigue as an Indicator of Eccentric Exercise-Induced Muscle Injury: The Role of Vitamin E
authors: Antonios Kyparos, Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Konstantina Dipla, Andreas Zafeiridis, Vassilis Paschalis,...
abstract: This study examined if vitamin E reduces eccentric exercise-induced muscle injury in rats, using low-frequency fatigue as an indicator. Vitamin E supplementation improved muscle force decline and recovery, suggesting it attenuates exercise-induced injury.

title: The effects of multi mineral-vitamin D and vitamins (C+E) supplementation in the prevention of preeclampsia: An RCT
authors: Milad Azami, Tayebe Azadi, Sepidezahra Farhang, Shoobo Rahmati, Khadijeh Pourtaghi
abstract: A randomized trial investigated multimineral-vitamin D and vitamins C+E supplementation in pregnant women. Multimineral-vitamin D significantly reduced preeclampsia incidence and neonatal complications compared to controls.

title: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a mixture of vitamin C and vitamin E for endurance capacity in a double blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Seung Wan Kang, Seokyung Hahn, Jung-Kyu Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Byung-Joo Park, Sang Chul Lee
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a vitamin C/E mixture were tested for endurance effects in exercising males. OLFE significantly improved running time and anaerobic threshold, while the vitamin mixture unexpectedly reduced VO2 max.

title: Isolated Soy Protein Supplementation Combined With Resistance Training Improves Muscle Strength, Mass, and Physical Performance of Aging Female Mice
authors: Mon-Chien Lee, Yi-Ju Hsu, Fang-Yu Wu, Chi-Chang Huang, Hsueh-Yu Li, Wen-Chyuan Chen
abstract: Isolated soy protein and resistance training were studied in aging female mice. Combining both interventions significantly improved muscle strength, mass, and physical performance.

title: Supplementation with  Lactiplantibacillus brevis  GKEX Combined with Resistance Exercise Training Improves Muscle Mass, Strength Performance, and Body Fat Condition in Healthy Humans
authors: Mon-Chien Lee, Yi-Ju Hsu, Chin-Shan Ho, You-Shan Tsai, Chin-Chu Chen, Chi-Chang Huang
abstract: This study investigated the effects of *Lactiplantibacillus brevis* GKEX supplementation combined with resistance training. The combination significantly improved muscle mass, strength, and reduced body fat compared to placebo.

title: Effects of gamma oryzanol supplementation on anthropometric measurements & muscular strength in healthy males following chronic resistance training
authors: Saghar Eslami, Norhaizan Mohd Esa, Seyed Mohammad Marandi, Gholamali Ghasemi, Sepehr Eslami
source: The Indian Journal of Medical Research
abstract: This study investigated gamma oryzanol supplementation's effects on strength and body measurements during resistance training. Gamma oryzanol improved muscular strength but did not significantly alter anthropometric measurements.

title: The effects of d-aspartic acid supplementation in resistance-trained men over a three month training period: A randomised controlled trial
authors: Geoffrey W. Melville, Jason C. Siegler, Paul W. M. Marshall
abstract: This study investigated the effects of d-aspartic acid supplementation on resistance-trained men over three months. D-aspartic acid did not alter testosterone levels but reduced estradiol, while both groups saw similar strength and muscle growth.

title: Potential harms of supplementation with high doses of antioxidants in athletes
authors: Shunchang Li, Babatunde Fasipe, Ismail Laher
abstract: This paper reviews the use of high-dose antioxidant supplements by athletes. It concludes that these supplements may hinder beneficial training adaptations and potentially cause harm.

title: Cross-Sectional Associations Between Dietary Antioxidant Vitamins C, E and Carotenoid Intakes and Sarcopenic Indices in Women Aged 18–79 Years
authors: A. A. Welch, A. Jennings, E. Kelaiditi, J. Skinner, C. J. Steves
abstract: This study examined the relationship between dietary antioxidant vitamin intake and sarcopenic indices in women. Higher vitamin C and carotenoid intake was associated with greater skeletal muscle mass and power, especially in younger women.

title: No Significant Differences in Muscle Growth and Strength Development When Consuming Soy and Whey Protein Supplements Matched for Leucine Following a 12 Week Resistance Training Program in Men and Women: A Randomized Trial
authors: Heidi M. Lynch, Matthew P. Buman, Jared M. Dickinson, Lynda B. Ransdell, Carol S. Johnston, Christop...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared soy and whey protein supplements matched for leucine in untrained individuals undergoing resistance training. No significant differences in muscle growth or strength development were found between the two protein groups.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of antioxidants with or without exercise training improving muscle condition in older adults
authors: Yijie Wang, Ziping He, Chunye Long, Yue Li, Yuzhe Yuan, Tianlong Huang
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of antioxidants and exercise on muscle condition in older adults. Combining antioxidants with exercise yielded greater improvements in muscle strength and physical function than either intervention alone.

title: Effects of dietary vitamin E on muscle vitamin E and fatty acid content in Aohan fine-wool sheep
authors: Kun Liu, Suyun Ge, Hailing Luo, Dubing Yue, Leyan Yan
source: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology
abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary vitamin E on muscle composition in Aohan fine-wool sheep. Vitamin E supplementation improved mutton's nutritional value by reducing saturated fatty acids and increasing monounsaturated fatty acids and conjugated linoleic acid, with optimal results at 200 IU/day.

title: Vitamin E in Sarcopenia: Current Evidences on Its Role in Prevention and Treatment
authors: Shy Cian Khor, Norwahidah Abdul Karim, Wan Zurinah Wan Ngah, Yasmin Anum Mohd Yusof, Suzana Makpol
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's potential role in preventing and treating sarcopenia, an age-related muscle loss syndrome. While promising antioxidant properties exist, current evidence for its direct impact on muscle health remains inconclusive.

title: Effects of low-dose ibuprofen supplementation and resistance training on bone and muscle in postmenopausal women: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Whitney R.D. Duff, Saija A. Kontulainen, Darren G. Candow, Julianne J. Gordon, Riley S. Mason, Regin...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training and ibuprofen on bone and muscle in postmenopausal women. Ibuprofen supplementation showed some benefits for bone health, particularly when combined with stretching.

title: Resistance Training Improves Muscle Strength and Function, Regardless of Protein Supplementation, in the Mid- to Long-Term Period after Gastric Bypass
authors: Gabriela S. Oliveira, Flávio T. Vieira, Fernando Lamarca, Ricardo M. Lima, Kênia M. B. Carvalho, Eli...
abstract: Resistance training was studied in individuals 2-7 years post-gastric bypass, with or without protein supplementation. Resistance training alone, or with protein, improved muscle strength and physical function.

title: Influence of vitamin D supplementation on muscle strength and exercise capacity in Mongolian schoolchildren: a randomised controlled trial
authors: Davaasambuu Ganmaa, Stephanie Hemmings, David A. Jolliffe, Uyanga Buyanjargal, Gantsetseg Garmaa, Un...
abstract: A randomized controlled trial investigated weekly vitamin D supplementation in Mongolian schoolchildren. The supplementation successfully increased vitamin D levels but did not improve muscle strength or exercise capacity.

title: Marginal vitamin C status is associated with reduced fat oxidation during submaximal exercise in young adults
authors: Carol S Johnston, Corinne Corte, Pamela D Swan
abstract: Marginal vitamin C status was studied in relation to fat oxidation during submaximal exercise. Low vitamin C status was associated with reduced fat oxidation, which was improved by vitamin C repletion.

title: Vitamin C and glutathione supplementation: a review of their additive effects on exercise performance
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
abstract: This review examined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation's effects on exercise performance. Combined supplementation's additive effects are anticipated but remain largely unexplored and require further study.

title: The effect of vitamin E supplementation on selected inflammatory biomarkers in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
authors: Omid Asbaghi, Mehdi Sadeghian, Behzad Nazarian, Mehrnoosh Sarreshtedari, Hassan Mozaffari-Khosravi, ...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E's effects on inflammatory biomarkers in adults. Vitamin E, especially alpha-tocopherol, significantly reduced C-reactive protein and tumor necrosis factor-alpha levels.

title: Well-Trained Elders Have Antioxidant Responses and an Equal Magnitude of EIMD as Young Adults
authors: Eva Tékus, Nikolett Lilla Szénási, Edina Szabó, Zoltan Heckel, Tibor Mintál, Tamas Kőszegi, Tamas At...
abstract: This study examined antioxidant responses and muscle damage markers in young and older men after eccentric training. No significant differences in antioxidant capacity or muscle damage were found between the groups, suggesting similar adaptability.

title: Vitamins C and E alleviate the deleterious effects of electronic cigarettes on tongue muscles and nerves in rat model
authors: Yasmine M. Tolba, Raghda A. Abou ayana, Dina A. Nagui
abstract: This study investigated electronic cigarette effects on rat tongue muscles and nerves, and the protective roles of vitamins C and E. Vitamins E and C, but not C alone, significantly mitigated electronic cigarette-induced oxidative damage and ultrastructural harm.

title: Protective Role of Vitamin C Intake on Muscle Damage in Male Adolescents Performing Strenuous Physical Activity
authors: Shreef G. N. Gabrial, Marie-Christine R. Shakib, Gamal N. Gabrial
source: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's effect on muscle damage in male adolescents during strenuous exercise. Vitamin C supplementation significantly reduced markers of muscle damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: Building strength, endurance, and mobility using an astaxanthin formulation with functional training in elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Amir S. Ali, Matthew D. Campbell, Kevin Kilroy, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: An astaxanthin formulation was tested with functional training in elderly subjects. The formulation improved muscle strength and size, in addition to exercise-induced gains in endurance and mobility.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Improves Handgrip Strength in Postmenopausal Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Jia-Li Zhang, Christina Chui-Wa Poon, Man-Sau Wong, Wen-Xiong Li, Yi-Xun Guo, Yan Zhang
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials on vitamin D supplementation and muscle function in postmenopausal women. Vitamin D supplementation significantly improved handgrip strength, indicating enhanced muscle strength.

title: Specific Collagen Peptides in Combination with Resistance Training Improve Body Composition and Regional Muscle Strength in Premenopausal Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Patrick Jendricke, Christoph Centner, Denise Zdzieblik, Albert Gollhofer, Daniel König
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training plus specific collagen peptides (SCP) on premenopausal women. SCP supplementation, combined with resistance training, significantly improved fat-free mass and hand-grip strength compared to placebo.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: The effects of nutritional supplementation on older sarcopenic individuals who engage in resistance training: a meta-analysis
authors: Zixian Song, Tingting Pan, Xu Tong, Ying Yang, Ze Zhang
abstract: This meta-analysis examined resistance training with nutritional supplementation for sarcopenia. Combining resistance training with supplements, particularly protein and vitamin D, improved grip strength in older adults with sarcopenia.

title: Elevated hepcidin serum level in response to inflammatory and iron signals in exercising athletes is independent of moderate supplementation with vitamin C and E
authors: Víctor Díaz, Ana B Peinado, Laura Barba-Moreno, Sandro Altamura, Javier Butragueño, Marcela González...
abstract: This study investigated hepcidin levels in athletes after exercise. Hepcidin remained elevated despite vitamin C and E supplementation, indicating these vitamins do not alter the response to inflammatory and iron signals.

title: The interaction effects of aerobic exercise training and vitamin D supplementation on plasma lipid profiles and insulin resistance in ovariectomized rats
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Rastegar Hoseini
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of aerobic exercise and vitamin D on ovariectomized rats. The combination significantly improved lipid profiles and reduced insulin resistance.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.

title: Beneficial Effects of  Asparagus officinalis  Extract Supplementation on Muscle Mass and Strength following Resistance Training and Detraining in Healthy Males
authors: Barakat Denben, Siriporn Sripinyowanich, Ratree Ruangthai, Jatuporn Phoemsapthawee
abstract: Asparagus officinalis extract was supplemented during resistance training and detraining in healthy males. The extract helped maintain muscle mass and strength during detraining by reducing cortisol levels.

title: Influence of Vitamin C Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Neutrophil Inflammatory Response in Acute and Regular Exercise
authors: Ljiljana M. Popovic, Nebojsa R. Mitic, Dijana Miric, Boban Bisevac, Mirjana Miric, Brankica Popovic
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's impact on oxidative stress and neutrophil inflammation from exercise. Vitamin C supplementation reduced exercise-induced lipid peroxidation but did not affect neutrophil inflammatory response.

title: Shatavari supplementation during eight weeks of resistance training increases training load, enhances skeletal muscle contractility and alters the skeletal muscle proteome in older women
authors: Elsa Greed, Jack Pritchard, Lauren Struszczak, Esra Bozbaş, Georgia Ek, Jordan Acheson, Ben Winney, ...
abstract: Shatavari supplementation was studied in older women undergoing resistance training. It increased training load, improved muscle relaxation speed, and altered muscle protein expression, suggesting reduced neuromuscular fatigue.

title: Powdered tart cherry supplementation surrounding a single bout of intense resistance exercise demonstrates potential attenuation of recovery strength decrement with no definitive oxidative or inflammatory effect
authors: K Levers, R Dalton, E Galvan, C Goodenough, A O'Connor, S Simbo, N Barringer, S Mertens-Talcott, C R...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effects of  Cistanche deserticola  Y.C. Ma Supplementation on Muscle Strength and Recovery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Biaoxu Tao, Weihao Lian, Rongrong Min, Xiaoyu Zhang, Liqi Chen, Sun Hao, Ze Li, Chengzhe Ma, Haojie ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of *Cistanche deserticola* supplementation on muscle strength and recovery in trained and untrained men. Supplementation significantly improved muscle strength, endurance, and recovery markers in both groups.
